description: Claude Code skills for equity investors and traders — market analysis, technical charting, economic calendars, screeners, and trading strategy development.
readmeExcerpt: Claude Trading Skills Claude Trading Skills started as a personal project to use AI to improve my own trading process. Claude Trading Skills is a Claude Skills-based trading workflow toolkit for time-constrained individual investors. It is designed for investors who use long-term investing, ETFs, and dividend stocks as their core, while using disciplined swing trading as a satellite strategy when market conditions are favorable. The goal is not to outsource buy/sell decisions to AI. The goal is to structure market review, risk management, trade planning, journaling, and continuous improvement. It is open source because the workflows, checklists, and review habits behind better trading decisions can improve through shared practice. This is not a signal service or a promise of profitability. It is a toolkit for traders who want to build a better decision process. The project follows a **first for self, open for others** stance: it is built first as a practical workflow the author uses, then shared openly for others who face similar constraints. 📖 **Documentation site:** **Project vision:** `PROJECT_VISION.md` 日本語版READMEは`README.ja.md`をご覧ください。 Disclaimer This repository is for educat

name: alibaba/open-code-review
description: Secure, fast, efficient, battle-tested at Alibaba's scale. Hybrid architecture code review tool: deterministic pipelines + LLM Agent, precise line-level comments, built-in multi-language ruleset (NPE, thread-safety, XSS, SQL injection), OpenAI & Anthropic compatible.
readmeExcerpt: OpenCodeReview English | 简体中文 | 日本語 | 한국어 | Русский What is Open Code Review? Open Code Review is an AI-powered code review CLI tool. It originated as Alibaba Group's internal official AI code review assistant — over the past two years, it has served tens of thousands of developers and identified millions of code defects. After thorough validation at massive scale, we incubated it into an open source project for the community. Simply configure a model endpoint to get started. It reads Git diffs, sends changed files to a configurable LLM via an agent with tool-use capabilities, and generates structured review comments with line-level precision. The agent can read full file contents, search the codebase, inspect other changed files for context, and produce deep reviews — not just surface-level diff feedback. Beyond diff review, `ocr scan` reviews entire files for auditing unfamiliar codebases or directories that have no meaningful diff. Visit the official website for more details. name: ashhart/TensorFold
description: LLM Inference Engine for Metal, CUDA and Vulkan.
readmeExcerpt: TensorFold TensorFold serves language models from a Zig binary on Apple Silicon and NVIDIA GPUs. The engine reads checkpoints, tokenizes requests and runs Metal or CUDA kernels directly. Serving needs no Python or MLX installation. Building with a coding agent? Have it load the contributor skill before it writes any code. Contributing with agents Please use Agent Traffic Control before editing TensorFold so contributors and agents can avoid duplicate work and conflicting changes. Check the live agent radar before choosing an issue and follow CONTRIBUTING.md and the ATC contributor instructions. Install or upgrade ATC to 0.9.4 or later, then run from an updated TensorFold clone: Replace `ISSUE` with the issue number and claim only after a complete check says the work is free. TensorFold enables automatic public check-ins: a successful new claim starts an anonymous session on the radar and returns its `session` number. Keep that number instead of starting a duplicate session. For work already yours, start a session with `atc start ISSUE --json`.
